text:
maria: Heads up — we've got a EU-west wave of WebSocket clients going silent for ~20–40s then mass reconnects. Dashboard shows an active_connections spike then sudden drop. Not the usual TTL churn.

maria: repro logs (conn-id=cn_9f3a):
```
[2026-03-21T10:12:04Z] conn=cn_9f3a state=OPEN last_frame=2026-03-21T10:12:01Z
[2026-03-21T10:12:25Z] conn=cn_9f3a state=HALT keepalive_missed=1
[2026-03-21T10:12:55Z] client reconnecting conn=cn_9f3a new_conn=cn_9f3a_1
```

maria: note: client keepalive is 15s. We see no CLOSE, no FIN from proxy. Just silence then client reconnects.

jack: can you paste headers and route info for that conn-id? suspect routing weight flip during canary rollout.

maria: headers: `x-routing-hint: eu-west-1b`, `x-route-version: v2-canary` and downstream proxy is occasionally returning `204` on reattach (seen in proxy logs).

sophie: telemetry shows an uptick of `proxy:midstream-204` in eu-west around 10:12. Also the per-route heartbeat metric `last_frame_received_seconds` has a gap for many connections.

anshu: are we double-counting for billing? reconnection storms could create duplicate billing tokens if resume-idempotency isn't deduped.

maria: we have customers reporting duplicate token usage counts. snippet from billing: `charge_event: session_resume token=tok_abc count=1` followed by immediate second `charge_event` for same token after reconnect.

jack: hypothesis — canary weight was ramped from 10%->60% at 10:10 and the proxy is performing a midflight route-swap. Some proxies reply 204 (no-session) instead of forwarding `REATTACH`, causing client to fallback and re-open. If client re-opens quickly we get double-charge.

oliver: FYI we rolled a console routing-weight change at 10:08 (canary push). We also pushed the new 'fast-failover' toggle. Might be related.

maria: repro steps: 1) open ws to v2-canary via edge proxy, 2) ramp canary weight to 60% (console), 3) observe silent stalls then reconnect flood. Repeated locally with a small script.

jack: immediate mitigations: 1) pause canary ramp and rollback weights, 2) add jitter before client reconnect (client SDK), 3) server-side dedupe for `session_resume` billing events for 5s window.

oliver: can we do a fast rollback from console now? I can flip weight back to 10% and disable fast-failover.

deploy-bot: canary rollback initiated by oliver — job #deploy-9201 queued. :spinner:

anshu: also adding alert to billing dashboard for duplicate token events and a Grafana panel for `last_frame_received_seconds` percentile by route.

sophie: +1 on adding `last_frame_received` metric and a trace sample exporter for connections that go HALT. That'll help isolate proxy vs client.

jack: long-term fixes: make reattach handling idempotent across proxies (RFC: reattach v2), ensure proxy returns 410 instead of 204 when session lost, and add route-swap drain window where we honor existing connections for N seconds.

maria: I opened an infra ticket: INFRA-3289 with logs and repro script. Dropping the script here: `./scripts/repro/ws-hang.sh --region eu-west --canary-weight 60 --concurrency 200`.

oliver: console UX follow-up — add a prominent warning when ramping weight that says "route swap may cause midstream reattaches for active sockets" + a one-click rollback.

maria: rolling back now confirms connection stability returns after ~2 mins. Will leave the rollback until we patch.

jack: assigning to eng-runtime to own the reattach idempotency. @jack will follow up with a PR for proxy semantics.

anshu: I've opened billing guard PR to dedupe resume tokens for 5s window.

sophie: I'll add the metric and an alert runbook.

maria: thanks everyone. filing a postmortem after INFRA-3289 is triaged. :thumbsup:
